A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching methods, equations, experiments, and figure/table correspondence despite the revised title. All 12 pages of each file are readable. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix; both end with references.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction experiments, video consistency evaluations, human ELO scores, architecture ablations, and qualitative generation results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 5–10.

after.justification: V4 retains the original experimental results, including reconstruction metrics, consistency measurements, human ELO scores, and qualitative ablation examples.

M1.justification: The random-frame pretraining procedure, noise masking, two-branch convolution/attention encoder, finetuning objectives, and autoregressive inference remain unchanged. V4 renames the memory compression model as a history encoder and explicitly restates encoder updates during finetuning, which v1 already described and illustrated.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Internet-video coverage, including vertical Short-style and horizontal videos, and evaluate frame reconstruction and storyboard-conditioned video generation. No dataset, domain, task, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparator sets match: the FramePack-equivalent Large Patchifier and encoder variants in Table 1, Wan-I2V plus Qwen-Edit with one, two, or three input images and the same ablations in Table 2, and the same HunyuanVideo/Wan configurations in Table 3.

E3.justification: Both retain 1000 storyboard prompts, 4096 unseen test videos, the same metrics and model configurations, and the 100k-step comparison with versus without pretraining. Removing the 20-second description from Figure 6's caption does not change the setting, which remains stated in Section 4.2 and the figure.

E4.justification: The encoder-branch, patchifier, compression-rate, and pretraining ablations are retained. The sliding-window, cross-attention, and multiple-encoder case studies in Figures 8–10 test the same questions using the same examples; no supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report metric point estimates and ELO scores without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V4 adds no uncertainty-estimation or statistical-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–3 match. For example, Proposed (4×4×2) retains PSNR 17.41, SSIM 0.596, and LPIPS 0.171 in Table 1 and ELO 1216 in Table 2. The qualitative examples and reported experimental findings are also retained.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same rectified-flow formulation, indexed reconstruction-distance objective, and pretraining/finetuning losses in Equations 1–4. No mathematical definition, formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is substantively added or revised.

C1.justification: V4 softens the abstract and conclusion's emphasis on high-fidelity reconstruction toward lightweight history features and content consistency for personal/local workflows. It adds an abstract claim of comparability to heavier alternatives and drops editing from the contribution list. The central two-stage video-generation contribution remains.

C2.justification: V4 more explicitly interprets pretraining as providing dense history coverage and finetuning as establishing generation-oriented consistency. Section 3.2 adds that continued encoder updates adapt features from frame-query targets toward that downstream goal. Existing drift observations and architecture trade-off discussions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Hardware, PyTorch/Accelerate usage, LoRA rank 128, encoder channel progression, compression conventions, and data-captioning instructions are unchanged. Encoder finetuning was already documented in v1; its explicit restatement supplies no new implementation setting. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: V4 removes Wang et al.'s 2004 SSIM paper, reference [60] in v1, while retaining SSIM evaluation. The remaining cited works match after renumbering, and the detailed related-work comparisons are substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are substantially rewritten around lightweight history encoding and the roles of the two training stages. Method descriptions, subsection headings, and recurring terminology are also revised. This is an extensive narrative rewrite despite the retained overall section order.

P2.justification: All ten figures and three tables are retained with matching scientific displays. Several captions and their emphasis formatting change, and Figures 3–4 move from separate columns to a vertical arrangement in the right column. Other differences mainly involve text and float reflow.

improvement.justification: V4 more clearly connects frame-query pretraining, continued encoder adaptation, and downstream content consistency, especially in the introduction and Section 3.2. This provides a limited explanatory improvement. The abstract and captions lose some quantitative specificity, but those details remain in diagrams and results; experimental support and reproducibility information are unchanged.
